We need to find template that when applied to the given molecule reproduces the DIBAL-H reduction: ester to aldehyde? The description: carbon-oxygen bond broken, another carbon-oxygen bond order changes from 2 to 1, forming aliphatic hydroxyls. So forward reaction: DIBAL-H reduces ester to aldehyde? Actually DIBAL-H reduces ester to aldehyde, breaking C=O double bond to C-O single? The forward reaction (synthetic) would be oxidation? Wait retrosynthetic step: we have product (aldehyde?) The given molecule appears to be a protected diol? Let's examine SMILES: C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO

It contains a lactone? Actually there is a carbonyl CC=O (aldehyde) inside ring? The molecule seems to have an aldehyde (CC=O) attached to ring. The DIBAL-H reduction would convert an ester to aldehyde, so the precursor would be an ester. So template should break C-O bond (the O of ester) and change C=O to C-O single (forming hydroxyl). So functional groups broken: carbonyl? Actually carbon-oxygen bond broken (the C-O single bond of ester). Formed: aliphatic hydroxyls. So we need to search templates with functional_groups_broken: "carboxylic esters"? maybe. Let's get available functional groups list.
